thread:
maya: 🚨 POC blocked — ACME On‑Prem in eu-west. Customer tried to pin model 'redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.2' and the API returns 404 'model not available in region'. Also we get bursts of 429s when they bump concurrency. Can we swarm? cc @sahil @olivia @ben

sahil: can you paste the request and the exact error payload? are they on Private (appliance) or Dedicated? pricing Q for ops: if we push them to Dedicated trial, need a quick cost estimate to share.

maya: Private appliance. Request example below and log snippet. customer says they used the model_version param to pin.

```bash
curl -s -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.2","input":"Summarize Q1 results"}' \
  https://private.acme.example/api/v1/generate
```

logs:
2026-03-20T14:12:07Z ERROR serve.router request_id=abc123 code=404 msg="ModelVersionNotAvailableInRegion: redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.2 not found for deployment eu-west-1"
2026-03-20T14:12:08Z WARN  serve.rate request_id=abc124 code=429 msg="rate limit exceeded: 100 rps"

olivia: quick take — v1.4.2 was marked deprecated in our hosted catalog for the on‑prem build at the time that appliance image was assembled. For Private, model artifacts must be compiled into the appliance image. two possibilities:
1) the artifact for 1.4.2 wasn't built/pushed to the private artifact registry for eu-west, so the runtime returns 404.
2) or the customer pinned a variant that we never compiled for that HW target.

ben: confirms olivia's note. The 2026-02 appliance image bundle includes up to 'redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.0'. v1.4.2 build failed in CI (quant step) and was skipped.
Options:
- short term: use a compatible pinned version 'redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.0' or remove the version pin so the routing falls back to the latest compatible variant.
- medium: trigger a private build for v1.4.2 (ETA ~2h once queued, depends on quantization queue).
- alternate: route that workload to Hosted/Dedicated while the artifact is built (requires customer approval for egress).

ben: sample config to enable automatic fallback in their client if model missing:

```json
{"model":"redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.2","fallback_policy":"compatible_variant"}
```

lucy: for sales pitch: if they go Dedicated trial we can estimate baseline costs for the requested concurrency. @ben can you give a rough monthly delta for a tiny trial (4 x A10G-equivalent) for 30 days? customer cares about predictable latency.

ben: rough calc: 4 GPUs reserved ~ $Xk/mo (internal calc). For a 30-day trial with 8/5 traffic it translates to approx $Yk. I'll DM exact numbers (depends on commitment and burst policy).

anna: security note — routing to Hosted/Dedicated requires we sign off on the outbound egress and DLP controls. Also the customer sent a security questionnaire; question 12 asks about data residency for inference. If we route to Hosted, we need documented controls.

maya: thanks. Also those 429s — are they genuine rate limits or just the appliance hitting worker_count? Customer says they scaled to 50 concurrent reqs and saw 429s after a few seconds.

ben: 429s on Private often mean hitting the local concurrency throttle. Check their agent config: `worker_count` and `max_token_rps`. By default Private appliance is conservative. Two quick fixes:
- bump worker_count in /etc/redwood/agent.conf and restart agent (low risk).
- scale horizontally by adding another appliance to the pool (requires infra changes).

olivia: also check the logs for KV cache errors — if the model mismatch causes repeated cold starts it can amplify RPS and trigger 429s. Example error we saw in their traces: 

2026-03-20T14:12:06Z ERROR model.load request_id=abc120 msg="artifact not found: redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.2"
2026-03-20T14:12:07Z INFO  model.fallback request_id=abc120 msg="no fallback configured"

deploy-bot: build queued for redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.2 artifact id=build/1800004350 (started by ben). ETA ~2h.

sahil: for the customer facing response — prioritize: (1) ask them to try v1.4.0 pin (2) enable "fallback_policy: compatible_variant" (3) if they need 1.4.2 specifically, let them know build ETA and expected downtime/latency impact. Also capture pricing delta if they pick Dedicated fallback.

maya: I'll ask ACME to switch to 'redwood-open-llama-7b@v1.4.0' now and enable fallback_policy. Also asking if they'd accept routing to Hosted for only that model while build completes — will update security Q.

anna: I'll prepare a short addendum for the security questionnaire explaining controls for temporary Hosted routing and DLP — linking the doc: https://on.redwood/inference/privacy-dlp (internal).

maya: thanks team. I'll update ACME and follow up once they test. If build completes earlier, can someone ping the thread? :pray!
